public_interview_synthesis: At the September 9 Goldman Sachs event, Devgan described AI agents as an additional subscription/consumption layer above physics-based tools. His thesis is that more design experiments and growing chip complexity sustain tool demand even when individual workflows accelerate. Hardware capacity and advanced-node interfaces were presented as additional drivers. These are management expectations; the interview does not supply a separately auditable AI revenue forecast. Source is a third-party transcript, with official event identity verified; audio was not independently transcribed.
call_QA_synthesis: Q2 discussion emphasized broad software/add-on demand, delivery timing in IP, hardware supply constraints, and investment in Intel opportunities and Hexagon integration. Management did not quantify an abrupt agentic-AI revenue step-up. The model therefore fades growth rather than treating product demonstrations or customer engagement counts as contracted sales.
